meta.medicalFacility:
Acute Care Services (ACS): For emergencies, dial 911. For other acute illnesses or injuries sustained during work hours, employees should seek treatment at the 31 CF Health Services Centre Detachment, located at 154 Jaeger Way, Building 154 Hornell Heights, Ontario P0H 1P0.

Emergency Room: Emergency services are available North Bay regional Health Centre at 50 College Dr, North Bay, ON P1B 5A4.

Civilian employees may choose to seek medical care from any provider, but they must comply with their health care plan’s provisions. Civilian employees are encouraged to seek duty-related medical care from nearby military medical facilities, as these are typically the closest and help to reduce Workers’ Compensation expenses.
meta.evacuationRoute:
Primary Evacuation Location: Parking lot closest to main turn style, within the GRA

Secondary Evacuation Location: Parking Lot across from Building 7A

1.	Secure all classified materials.

2.	Leave lights on.

3.	Close doors, but keep doors unlocked.

4.	Ensure that all building occupants received the notification to evacuate through means of Fire Alarm, Phone, Radio, Word of mouth, Etc.

5.	Evacuate to your Primary or Alternate Evacuation Location as directed by the Fire Dept or the Incident Commander.  The highest-ranking member shall ensure an orderly evacuation. No critical operations. All personnel will evacuate. 

6.	Do not transmit on radios within 300 feet of the building (bomb threat situations).

7.	Highest ranking member will assemble all Safety Personnel at the Evacuation Location and account for all personnel. 

8.	Notify the Command, Fire Dept. or Incident Commander of your Personnel Accountability.
meta.shelterInPlace:
The SIP Room is your personal work center, or as defined by CADS leadership.

1.	Alert all building occupants to complete their Building Shelter-In-Place tasks.

2.	Get all your personnel inside the building.

3.	Close all exterior and interior doors. Close and lock all windows.

4.	Shut down the building HVAC system.

5.	Duct tape plastic sheeting around all exterior windows and vents.

6.	Duct tape around exterior doors.  Place wet towels over the crack at the bottom of the exterior doors.

7.	Secure all classified materials.

8.	Move to the most interior room(s) in your building. This is your SAFE ROOM.

9.	Seal the safe room doors with duct tape.

10.	Once the Building Shelter-In-Place tasks have been completed, notify Command.  Report your building number and the number of personnel that you have sheltered.

11.	Follow all emergency directions provided by the Command Post.

12.	Tune to the local radio or television for additional information.

13.	Perform First Aid as necessary.

14.	Wait for the “ALL CLEAR” to be issued by the Command Post before resuming normal operations.  Evacuate the building.  Emergency Response personnel will determine if the building needs to be ventilated.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Local Traffic Hazards:

North Bay has numerous road hazards, including unimproved dirt roads, paved roads with poor shoulders, and adverse weather conditions such as wind/dust storms and snow/ice, which can lead to vehicle rollovers. Rollovers on Highway 11, especially during snow/black ice conditions. Personnel should reduce speed and prepare for slick roads. It is recommended to check road conditions before traveling, especially in winter weather. Road reports can be accessed at http://511on.ca/.
meta.trafficContacts:
Motorcycle Operator Training:

Military personnel who operate or intend to operate a motorcycle on a roadway, government-owned or leased motorcycles, and Air Force civilian personnel required to operate a motorcycle must complete motorcycle safety training. This training is mandatory for motorcycles with engine displacements of over 49cc unless specified otherwise by state, territory, host nation, or applicable SOFA requirements.

Motorcycle safety training does not substitute for state licensing requirements. Riders must possess a valid motorcycle license, endorsement, or rider’s permit before operating a motorcycle on roadways, including travel to and from training locations.
All newly assigned personnel must complete the commander’s initial motorcycle safety briefing within 30 duty days of assignment or identification as a rider. Personnel transferring out will complete out-processing through the motorcycle safety representative to transfer their record in the MUSTT/Training module. Motorcycle riders are required to attend an annual/pre-season motorcycle safety briefing.

Please contact USR if planning to operate motorcycle.
